lessons.title: Lesson 1: MVC Architecture
lessons.html:
Model-View-Controller Pattern

MVC separates concerns: Model (data), View (UI), Controller (logic). Makes code maintainable.

Structure:

  • Model: Database operations, business logic
  • View: HTML templates
  • Controller: Handles requests, coordinates Model+View
class UserController {
    public function index() {
        $model = new UserModel();
        $users = $model->getAll();
        require 'views/users/index.php';
    }
}

Benefits: Reusable components, easier testing, team collaboration.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Composer & Dependencies
lessons.html:
PHP Package Manager

Composer manages libraries and autoloading. Like npm for PHP.

{
    "require": {
        "monolog/monolog": "2.*",
        "vlucas/phpdotenv": "^5.0"
    },
    "autoload": {
        "psr-4": {
            "App\": "src/"
        }
    }
}
$ composer install
$ composer require guzzlehttp/guzzle  // Add new package

Autoloading:

require 'vendor/autoload.php';
$logger = new Monolog Logger('app');
$logger->info('User logged in');

lessons.title: Lesson 3: PDO Advanced
lessons.html:
Secure Database Operations

PDO with prepared statements prevents SQL injection. Always use!

CRUD Examples:

// CREATE
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)');
$stmt->execute(['John', 'john@example.com']);
$userId = $pdo->lastInsertId();

// READ
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?');
$stmt->execute([$userId]);
$user = $stmt->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);

Transactions:

$pdo->beginTransaction();
try {
    $pdo->exec('UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1');
    $pdo->exec('UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2');
    $pdo->commit();
} catch (Exception $e) {
    $pdo->rollBack();
}

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Sessions & Authentication
lessons.html:
User Sessions & Login System

Sessions track logged-in users across requests.

<?php
session_start();

// Login
if ($_POST && authenticate($_POST['email'], $_POST['password'])) {
    $_SESSION['user_id'] = $user['id'];
    $_SESSION['user_name'] = $user['name'];
    header('Location: dashboard.php');
}

Protected Pages:

<?php
session_start();
if (!isset($_SESSION['user_id'])) {
    header('Location: login.php');
    exit;
}

Security: Use password_hash(), password_verify(), HTTPS.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: RESTful APIs
lessons.html:
Building JSON APIs

APIs return JSON data for frontend apps, mobile, etc.

header('Content-Type: application/json');

switch ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD']) {
    case 'GET':
        if (isset($_GET['id'])) {
            echo json_encode(getUser($_GET['id']));
        } else {
            echo json_encode(getAllUsers());
        }
        break;
    case 'POST':
        $data = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
        echo json_encode(createUser($data));
        break;
}

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Templating with Twig
lessons.html:
Modern PHP Templating

Twig separates logic from presentation. Much cleaner than mixing PHP in HTML.

{# template.twig #}
<h1>Welcome, {{ user.name }}!</h1>
<ul>
{% for post in posts %}
    <li>{{ post.title }} - {{ post.created|date('Y-m-d') }}</li>
{% endfor %}</ul>
$loader = new Twig Loader FilesystemLoader(__DIR__ . '/templates');
$twig = new Twig Environment($loader);
echo $twig->render('user.twig', [
    'user' => $currentUser,
    'posts' => $userPosts
]);

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Deployment & Docker
lessons.html:
Production Deployment

Containerize apps with Docker for consistent environments.

FROM php:8.2-apache
COPY . /var/www/html/
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y 
    default-mysql-client
RUN docker-php-ext-install pdo_mysql
EXPOSE 80

docker-compose.yml:

version: '3'
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
  db:
    image: mysql:8.0
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: secret
